correctness.rationale: For five-site positive nilpotent complex shifts, the Haar-shadow determinant equality reduces exactly to S=sum x_j=1+q and Q=x1x3+x1x4+x2x4=q after scaling by 2lambda1. Minimizing operator norm is minimizing t=max x_j. The cap-constrained matching quadratic has a piecewise exact lower envelope Q_min=2St-5t^2 for S/4<=t<=S/3 and t(S-2t) for S/3<=t<=S/2; its equality cases give the two lower-q branches and strict-positive nonattainment. A bipartite singular-value Rayleigh quotient proves q<=max(x1,x4)<=t, attained iff x1=x4=q and positive middle weights exist, giving high-q branch. Checked actual CHECK.py and independent numerical allocations/Q_min tests; samples are not used as global proofs. Endpoints q_star and 1/3 and topology of minimizers (two, one, interval) are accounted for.
